title: Format Project Label
prompt: A TypeScript admin screen shows compact labels for projects. Write a typed function that returns the title followed by the id in parentheses.

explanation.beginner:
Example: formatProjectLabel({"id":"a1","title":"Alpha"}) produces "Alpha (a1)". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “uses the provided id”: input [{"id":"b2","title":"Beta"}] produces "Beta (b2)". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “uses the provided id”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
